La conferenza stampa di Giovanni Stroppa
10/10/2026
A due giorni dalla sfida contro l’Atalanta, valida per la sesta giornata del Campionato di Serie A Enilive 2026/27, il tecnico Giovanni Stroppa in conferenza stampa ha così anticipato le tematiche del match, in programma lunedì 12 ottobre alle ore 18.30 alla New Balance Arena di Bergamo.
Giovanni Stroppa, allenatore Venezia FC.
“La sosta ci ha dato la possibilità di recuperare parecchi giocatori e questa è sicuramente una bellissima notizia. Questi recuperi ci hanno permesso, in particolare nell’ultima settimana, di lavorare veramente bene. Il lavoro di queste settimane è stato finalizzato a consolidare e migliorare ciò che stavamo già facendo. Le amichevoli, in particolare quella in Croazia, ci hanno anche dato la possibilità di ruotare, valutare tutti i calciatori e far crescere in autostima e consapevolezza anche i ragazzi che in queste prime partite hanno trovato meno spazio. Nel complesso è stata un’ottima sosta, abbiamo migliorato la nostra mentalità e ci sono davvero tanti aspetti positivi da cui poter ripartire.
La partita contro l’Atalanta si affronta con la nostra identità, che non è mai mancata e anzi, anche nella partita con la Lazio, abbiamo dimostrato una notevole crescita sotto questo aspetto. Poi è chiaro che bisogna limare gli errori, nel non prendere dei gol e nella capacità di farli. Per quanto riguarda le prestazioni c’è soddisfazione, non soltanto da parte mia ma anche dei calciatori, ora bisogna andare a migliorare i numeri che sono fondamentali e una classifica che non ci vede protagonisti come la squadra meriterebbe. Lunedì avremo di fronte a noi una squadra di qualità, la cui classifica non rispecchia le ottime prestazioni che hanno fatto. Noi dovremo lavorare di squadra sugli episodi e sui dettagli perché loro hanno grande qualità anche nei singoli.
Io sento tutti i giorni fiducia nei miei confronti, da parte della squadra e da parte della società. Sento una fiducia impagabile, anche girando per strada e parlando con i tifosi. Vedo la squadra migliorare ogni giorno sotto l’aspetto dell’atteggiamento e del carattere, così come a livello tecnico e questo mi dà tanta ulteriore fiducia. Tutti noi siamo amareggiati per la classifica, ma i segnali e le risposte ci sono ogni giorno. Questa lunga sosta mi dà l’impressione che ci sia una voglia di tornare in campo straordinaria nei ragazzi e anche i calciatori che sono andati in Nazionale sono tornati veramente motivati”.

Atalanta vs. Venezia: both sides need a win
Atalanta look to bounce back after three straight defeats, while Venezia chase their first points of the season.
Atalanta and Venezia meet in the penultimate fixture of Matchday 6 in Serie A. The hosts need to respond after three consecutive defeats against Roma, Cagliari and Juventus if they are to stay in reach of the leading pack. Venezia, meanwhile, are still without a point and urgently need to get off the mark before their difficult start to the season becomes even more complicated.
HEAD TO HEAD
There have been 26 previous competitive meetings between the two sides in Bergamo: 15 wins for Atalanta (most recently 2-0 in the 2021/22 Coppa Italia), 6 draws (most recently 0-0 in Serie A 2024/25) and 5 wins for Venezia (most recently 3-0 in Serie B 1994/95).
Atalanta are unbeaten in their last 5 matches against Venezia (at the Gewiss Stadium and the Penzo): 4 wins and 1 draw. Their last defeat came on 1 February 2004 (Venezia-Atalanta 1-0, Serie B).
DID YOU KNOW?
Atalanta are one of just 2 teams to have received a red card, alongside Genoa.
Atalanta are one of 3 teams to have completed the fewest crosses (17, level with Cagliari and Lecce).
Only Frosinone (102) and Cagliari (99) have conceded more shots than Atalanta (91).
Only Parma (39), Lecce (41), Torino (45) and Cagliari (55) have attempted fewer shots than Atalanta (59, level with Genoa).
Venezia have gone 451 minutes without scoring in Bergamo: their last goal there was scored by Cerbone in the 89th minute of Atalanta-Venezia 0-3 on 25 September 1994 in Serie B.
Venezia also started the 2001/02 Serie A season with 5 defeats from their opening 5 Matchdays, a campaign that eventually ended in relegation to Serie B.
Venezia have lost 7 consecutive Serie A matches across the end of the 2024/25 season and the start of 2026/27. Their last positive result came on 12 May 2025 (Venezia-Fiorentina 2-1).
Venezia have received more yellow cards than any other team (16).
Venezia have conceded more goals than any other team overall (13), as well as the most in the opening 15 minutes of the second half (3, level with Udinese and Monza) and in the final 15 minutes of matches (4, level with Genoa).
Only Roma (68) have made more high turnovers than Venezia (64).
COACHES and PLAYERS
This will be the 2nd official meeting between Maurizio Sarri and Giovanni Stroppa: in their only previous encounter, the current Atalanta coach recorded a win (Spezia-Empoli 1-3, Serie B 2013/14).
Only Wladimiro Falcone (27) has made more saves than Marco Carnesecchi (24).
DISCIPLINE

Cautioned: none

It might be a stretch to call it a title defence. But it does have the feeling of a kind of homecoming.
Poland's Hubert Hurkacz returns to the Rolex Shanghai Masters this week for the first time since winning the 2023 title, having missed the past two editions due to injury.
Three years ago, the former World No. 6 survived a match point in the final to defeat Andrey Rublev 6-3, 3-6, 7-6(8) to claim his second ATP Masters 1000 title (Miami, 2021).
“I’ve been missing Shanghai a lot. I’m happy to finally be back,” Hurkacz said. “A lot of things have happened since then, but I’m feeling good and playing better tennis.
“It was crazy. It was a really amazing experience and definitely very challenging and difficult. I was not having my best season back then, so to turn it around with an amazing title, that was really fantastic.”
Since winning Shanghai, Hurkacz has taken just one title (the 2024 Estoril Open) as he has battled a series of injuries and indifferent form.
In 2025, he played just 26 matches. His last match came in June before he underwent surgery on his right knee in July, an injury he initially suffered at Wimbledon the year before.
In 2026, he started strongly with Top 10 wins over Alexander Zverev and Taylor Fritz to help lead Poland to victory in the United Cup, but he then won just one match for the remainder of the hard-court season through the Miami Open.
Solid, if not spectacular, results began in the clay swing and now he’s on the verge of reclaiming a spot in the Top 30 for the first time since April 2025 after a hot start in Asia.
After a final appearance in Chengdu and a semi-final showing this week in Beijing, where he retired with injury against Alex de Minaur, Hurkacz said that he’s very happy with his game.
“I think the form is really, really good,” he said. “I’ve been playing my best tennis in a long while.
“Things are on an upward trajectory. The body… I’m recovering well and doing everything I can to be 100 per cent fit for the match [here in Shanghai].”
The 29-year-old is now working with Gilles Cervara, the former longtime coach of Daniil Medvedev.
“Everyone’s different and has their different style. I really like what we’re doing together with Gilles,” said the eight-time ATP Tour champion. “He really takes care of things and also the details on the practice court. And I think it starts to show in the way I play.
“He writes a lot of notes. He’s written many books already.
“We changed a bit the way I practice and we have a focus on the quality of the shots and the adjustments to the ball. I think that allows me to maybe play a bit better, a bit stronger from the baseline.
“I definitely think that still the best years are to come, especially with the game and the potential that I have.”
Hurkacz plays his opening match Thursday against James Duckworth, with the winner to face four-time Shanghai champion Novak Djokovic, who on Tuesday won his seventh Beijing title.

Atalanta vs. Venezia: both sides need a win
Atalanta look to bounce back after three straight defeats, while Venezia chase their first points of the season.
Atalanta and Venezia meet in the penultimate fixture of Matchday 6 in Serie A. The hosts need to respond after three consecutive defeats against Roma, Cagliari and Juventus if they are to stay in reach of the leading pack. Venezia, meanwhile, are still without a point and urgently need to get off the mark before their difficult start to the season becomes even more complicated.
HEAD TO HEAD
There have been 26 previous competitive meetings between the two sides in Bergamo: 15 wins for Atalanta (most recently 2-0 in the 2021/22 Coppa Italia), 6 draws (most recently 0-0 in Serie A 2024/25) and 5 wins for Venezia (most recently 3-0 in Serie B 1994/95).
Atalanta are unbeaten in their last 5 matches against Venezia (at the Gewiss Stadium and the Penzo): 4 wins and 1 draw. Their last defeat came on 1 February 2004 (Venezia-Atalanta 1-0, Serie B).
DID YOU KNOW?
Atalanta are one of just 2 teams to have received a red card, alongside Genoa.
Atalanta are one of 3 teams to have completed the fewest crosses (17, level with Cagliari and Lecce).
Only Frosinone (102) and Cagliari (99) have conceded more shots than Atalanta (91).
Only Parma (39), Lecce (41), Torino (45) and Cagliari (55) have attempted fewer shots than Atalanta (59, level with Genoa).
Venezia have gone 451 minutes without scoring in Bergamo: their last goal there was scored by Cerbone in the 89th minute of Atalanta-Venezia 0-3 on 25 September 1994 in Serie B.
Venezia also started the 2001/02 Serie A season with 5 defeats from their opening 5 Matchdays, a campaign that eventually ended in relegation to Serie B.
Venezia have lost 7 consecutive Serie A matches across the end of the 2024/25 season and the start of 2026/27. Their last positive result came on 12 May 2025 (Venezia-Fiorentina 2-1).
Venezia have received more yellow cards than any other team (16).
Venezia have conceded more goals than any other team overall (13), as well as the most in the opening 15 minutes of the second half (3, level with Udinese and Monza) and in the final 15 minutes of matches (4, level with Genoa).
Only Roma (68) have made more high turnovers than Venezia (64).
COACHES and PLAYERS
This will be the 2nd official meeting between Maurizio Sarri and Giovanni Stroppa: in their only previous encounter, the current Atalanta coach recorded a win (Spezia-Empoli 1-3, Serie B 2013/14).
Only Wladimiro Falcone (27) has made more saves than Marco Carnesecchi (24).
